The data clearly distinguish the two hypotheses:

- **Z2Z1_Core_bottom**: cooling setpoint 24.61→23.57 °C in occupied hours, but **also** unoccupied setback setpoints shifted down ~1 °C (e.g., night 26.7→25.7, evening 24.84→23.8), and the heating setpoint shifted down ~1 °C at all hours likewise (19.77→18.87, night 15.6→14.6).
- **Z3Z1_Core_mid / Z4Z1_Core_top**: setpoints and temperatures essentially unchanged (dT ≤ 0.07 °C, dCP ≈ 0).

A uniform ~1 °C shift applied to **every** setpoint level (occupied and unoccupied, cooling and heating) of a single zone is the signature of a flat setpoint offset — i.e., a local override/controller offset. A schedule change would alter only the occupied-hours setpoint values while leaving the setback level intact.
